description: The DEDDIAG Python loader retrieves domestic appliance measurements and event annotations from a PostgreSQL instance containing the DEDDIAG dataset. The Rosenheim research team documents a command-line overview, labelled NumPy output and Python objects for selecting measurements and annotations by item and time interval. GitHub and PyPI provide the package, and the own README and repository metadata explicitly state MIT with free access. Its source dataset covers 15 German homes at 1 Hz, but actual retrieval coverage follows the imported records and requested interval. The loader can prepare calibration and benchmarking inputs for appliance-demand simulations, complementing datasets such as data-uk-dale-domestic-appliance-level-electricity. A caveat is that it requires the DEDDIAG database layout and is not documented as a universal reader for other smart-meter collections. Expanded or labelled outputs must retain the dataset's missing-data and annotation conventions. Only metadata and examples were inspected; no database connection was created and the package was not installed or executed.
